To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a novel approach to synthesize Pdn metal clusters with a controlled n value of ca. 12 by the cage templated synthesis.
the synthesis of hollow silica spheres with Pd12 clusters incarcerated within their voids is a novel approach to the preparation of metal nanoclusters with well defined n values.

we have developed a new approach to synthesize hollow silica nanoparticles with Pd12L12 and Pd12L16 metal clusters as the cores and that these metal clusters can be reduced to Pd(n) metal clusters (Figure S3 in Supporting Information).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new materials for use in chemical sensors.
the development of new methods for the synthesis of metal nanoclusters.
the preparation of metal nanoclusters with well defined n values and their use as catalysts in the selective oxidation of alkenes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Pd12L12 complex was successfully used as a template for silica hollow nanoparticles with a Pd12 core.
the Pd12L12 core is successfully incorporated in the silica framework and is not affected by the calcination process, which is in agreement with the results from XAFS and TEM.
the synthesis of hollow silica particles containing Pd clusters is a novel and unique approach to prepare metal clusters with small and well defined n values.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Pd12L 24 complex is a good model to understand the catalytic properties of the small Pdn clusters.
we have developed a new approach for the preparation of metal nanoclusters with strictly controlled numbers of metal centers.
we have developed a novel approach for the preparation of metal clusters of small n values.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have demonstrated a unique approach to incarcerate metal clusters with small number of metal atoms within the voids of hollow silica nanoparticles, which can serve as a new platform to investigate the properties of metal clusters with small numbers of metal atoms.
the Pd12L12 core can be successfully incarcerated into the hollow silica nanoparticle and the Pd12 cluster can be retained after calcination to give (Pdo)n oxide clusters.

we can use the voids of the hollow silica nanoparticles to incarcerate small number of metal centers, and we can also use this void space to synthesize metal nanoparticles with well defined numbers of metal atoms.
